narrative.overview:
Doctopus uses a centered, flat documentation canvas and a practical operating workspace. Typography, quiet dividers and restrained surface changes organize the interface. The violet octopus assets retain the product identity, with Violet as the default complete palette in Reader, Studio and the public demo configuration; published branding and the prepared alternate palettes remain supported.

Documentation prioritizes reading and understanding. The playground and Studio prioritize completing real tasks, with labeled forms, meaningful tables and explicit states. This is the Doctopus project system: its documented patterns describe the implemented reader and Studio rather than a universal interface template.
keyCharacteristics: Centered documentation shell with an unboxed article.
Shared local typefaces, palette roles and native controls.
Separate request/response examples and adjustable workspace tracks.
Flat surfaces with depth reserved for overlays.

rules.name: Resolved Palette
rules.body: Use the resolved palette for body text, inputs, tables and examples. Derive accent and syntax text against the actual background and surface rather than using raw brand colors as text.

rules.name: Independent Appearance
rules.body: Keep theme, appearance and documentation layout as separate preferences. System is the default appearance and follows OS changes live; Reader follows the OS before JavaScript and when JavaScript is unavailable through `color-scheme` and `light-dark()`. Explicit Light or Dark overrides appearance without changing the selected theme.

rules.name: Content Before Containers
rules.body: Keep the reading article and workspace shell flat. Use borders and surfaces to group actual controls, examples, data and focused tasks.

dos: Do preserve Doctopus naming and the violet octopus identity assets.
Do apply published or prepared palette roles consistently to text, controls, tables and code.
Do keep labels, descriptions, required/type metadata and explicit operational states visible where they are needed.
Do preserve keyboard and pointer resizing, native dialog behavior, clipboard fidelity, folding and fullscreen behavior.
Do keep table overflow local, focusable and labeled, and preserve localization and text zoom.
donts: Don't wrap the main reading article in a decorative card.
Don't add decorative kickers to the settings heading or promote leftover eyebrow selectors into a reusable pattern.
Don't replace meaningful tables with narrow mobile cards or hide columns to fit the viewport.
Don't add nonfunctional assistant controls, decorative dashboard charts or invented product claims.
Don't introduce font CDN or icon runtime requests.
